violations.description: Repository is missing a .gitignore file, leading to tracked temporary and sensitive files (.env and __pycache__/).
violations.evidence: .gitignore does not exist, and .env and __pycache__/app.cpython-311.pyc are tracked in version control.
violations.recommendation: Add a .gitignore file ignoring .env, __pycache__/, and other build/local artifacts, and remove them from git tracking.

violations.description: Temporary or generated build artifacts (bytecode cache) and local environment/secret files are tracked in version control.
violations.recommendation: Remove generated and environment files from git tracking and add them to .gitignore.

violations.description: Dependencies in requirements.txt lack version constraints (unpinned).
violations.evidence: requirements.txt contains unpinned dependencies: flask and requests.
violations.recommendation: Pin dependency versions or use a lockfile to ensure reproducible builds.

violations.description: Tests command in CI uses '|| true', masking test failures and making CI an ineffective quality gate.
violations.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs '- run: pytest || true', preventing test failures from failing the CI job.
violations.recommendation: Remove '|| true' so that failing tests correctly fail the CI build.

violations.description: CI workflow triggers only on push and lacks pull_request triggers.
violations.recommendation: Add pull_request trigger to run CI checks on pull requests.

violations.description: Hardcoded credentials/secrets committed directly in source and configuration files (.env and config.py).
violations.evidence: .env contains SECRET_TOKEN and config.py contains hardcoded AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and DB_PASSWORD.
violations.recommendation: Remove hardcoded secrets from code, use environment variables or a secure vault, and rotate compromised secrets.

violations.description: GitHub Actions workflow uses excessively broad 'write-all' permissions at the top level.
violations.recommendation: Apply principle of least privilege by specifying exact required permissions per job or workflow.

violations.description: The GitHub Actions workflow uses the dangerous pull_request_target trigger combined with checking out the pull request's head SHA (ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}), allowing untrusted code from pull requests to execute with elevated privileges and potential access to repository secrets.
violations.evidence:
pull_request_target:
    branches: [main]
...
      - uses: actions/checkout@main
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
violations.recommendation: Use the standard pull_request trigger instead of pull_request_target, or do not check out and execute untrusted head code under pull_request_target.

violations.description: settings.ini contains a hardcoded machine-specific absolute path (/Users/alice/dev/service-b/.cache), which breaks portability across different development environments or CI runners.
violations.recommendation: Use relative paths, environment variables, or platform-appropriate configuration paths.

violations.description: Actions/checkout is pinned to a mutable branch reference (@main) instead of a specific commit SHA or immutable tag.
violations.recommendation: Pin actions to an immutable commit SHA (e.g. actions/checkout@11bd71901ebe5b168054d32650f06180eec08a51) or tagged version.

violations.description: Tests exist in the repository (tests/test_service.py) but the CI workflow only runs ruff check and never executes pytest or tests.
violations.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs only 'ruff check .' and does not run pytest or test commands.
violations.recommendation: Add a test step running pytest to the CI pipeline.
